info.title: Genshin Impact API
info.description:
The Genshin Impact API, as it is actually registered.
Generated from the running route table by backend/generate-api-spec.php and
frontend/generate-openapi.mjs - not maintained by hand, and not annotated
onto the handlers. Regenerate with `npm run api` in frontend/.

AdminSiteSetting.description: One switch, as the admin form sees it. `type` is what makes the form generic: a new setting is a row in a migration and two translation keys, not a new field on this class and a new control in that template. `value` is text whatever the type says, because that is how the column stores it - the form parses on the way in and the API validates on the way back.

ApiError.title: ApiError
ApiError.description: What a failed request carries, whatever the status.

code.description: A stable name for the refusal, on the few that the caller has to tell apart rather than merely show. `error` is prose meant for a person and may be reworded at any time, so a page that has to *do* something different - send somebody to sign in again rather than just say no - reads this instead. Absent on every refusal where the message is the whole answer. invalid_token     no access token, or one that is expired or not ours (401) reauth_required   the action wants a sign-in at the IAM from the last ten minutes, and this one is older (403) maintenance       the site is closed to everybody but its admins (503) route_locked      an admin has switched that part of the site off (423)

AssetCatalogueCounts.title: AssetCatalogueCounts
AssetCatalogueCounts.description: How far the `files` table has drifted from the disk. `uncatalogued` is the number worth watching: files that turned up without going through the API, which is what happens when somebody uses FTP.

uncatalogued.description: On disk with no row. The check button adopts these.

unfiled.description: Of those, the ones in a folder no category claims.

missing.description: Rows whose file has gone. Reported, never deleted automatically.

AssetCleanupFile.title: AssetCleanupFile
AssetCleanupFile.description: One file that could go, and what it would give back.

AssetCleanupPage.title: AssetCleanupPage
AssetCleanupPage.description: A page of what a cleanup would remove. Paged because there are forty thousand of them and the point of showing the list at all is that somebody can take things out of it before agreeing.

bytes.description: What the whole set would give back, not just this page.

AssetCleanupProgress.title: AssetCleanupProgress
AssetCleanupProgress.description: How far a cleanup has got. Batched, like the conversion, for the same reason.

kept.description: Deselected in the modal, and therefore never queued.

failures.description: The first few that would not move.

AssetCleanupRequest.title: AssetCleanupRequest
AssetCleanupRequest.description: A batch of the cleanup the Files page drives. `keep` is what was deselected, not what to delete. The candidate list runs to tens of thousands and the handful somebody took out of it is the part worth sending; the server works out the rest against the catalogue as it is now rather than as the modal saw it a minute ago.

AssetConversionCount.title: AssetConversionCount
AssetConversionCount.description: One medium's conversion health. `missing` is work an encoder can do. `converted_only` is not: a PNG decoded back out of an AVIF is a bigger copy of the lossy one, not the original, so those are reported and left alone.

sources.description: Groups holding a source this medium can be converted from.

can_convert.description: False when nothing on this box can write the target format.

reclaimable.description: Originals that could actually be removed now: a source with a converted twin that nothing in the database still names. The exact count the cleanup modal lists, and what the delete button is gated on.

AssetConvertProgress.title: AssetConvertProgress
AssetConvertProgress.description: How far the conversion has got. The work is a queue on disk worked through a batch per request, so this is both the answer to "convert some more" and to "where are we".

skipped.description: Already there, or gone, by the time its turn came.

blocked.description: Left out of the queue because this box cannot write that format.

failures.description: The first few that would not convert, to see a pattern by.

AssetConvertRequest.title: AssetConvertRequest
AssetConvertRequest.description: A batch of the conversion the Files page drives. `restart` builds the work list, which is the walk over the whole tree; without it the next batch is taken off the list already there. That split is what lets seven thousand files be converted behind a progress bar rather than behind one request nobody can wait for. `limit` is a ceiling, not a promise: a batch also stops on a clock, so a queue of voice lines does not run for a minute because a queue of icons would have finished in fifty milliseconds.

url.description: The path the site loads it by, e.g. `assets/materials/Foo.avif`.

file_id.description: Its row in the catalogue, or null while the catalogue has not caught up.

category.description: The category it is filed under, by code.

AssetFolder.title: AssetFolder
AssetFolder.description: What /api/files and the upload endpoints answer with. None of this is in a database. The files on disk are the record, and these endpoints walk the folder rather than a table.

extension.description: Lower case, with no dot. `(none)` for a file with no extension.

age.description: Seconds since the survey was walked, so the page can say how stale it is.

catalogue.description: How far the `files` table has drifted from the disk.

AssetTrashResult.title: AssetTrashResult
AssetTrashResult.description: Deleting moves the file to the trash under a stamped name; nothing is lost.

url.description: Same as `path`, relative to the site root.

AuditLogEntry.title: AuditLogEntry
AuditLogEntry.description: One logged change. Two things differ from the `audit_logs` row: the username is joined in, and `changes` is decoded - the column stores it as JSON text.

entity_table.description: What the changed row belongs to, which is the row itself unless it is a child - a talent's cost says `characters` and the character's id, so one filter gives the whole history of one thing. Null on entries written before the columns existed whose row has since been replaced.

session_id.description: The sign-in it was made from, which is what knows the address and the browser and can be revoked: the IAM's session id (`sid`) - or, for entries from before the move to the IAM, the old numeric one, which the IAM kept. Null for anything with no session behind it - a migration, a sweep, a file found on disk.

changes.description: Column to { old, new }. Absent on an insert, which logs the whole row.

AuditLogUser.title: AuditLogUser
AuditLogUser.description: An account, reduced to what the audit filter needs to name it.

SiteSettingChange.title: SiteSettingChange
SiteSettingChange.description: What the site settings form sends back. The whole form in one request rather than a request per switch. Maintenance mode and the words on the maintenance page are one decision, and saving them separately leaves a window - however short - where the site is closed and the sign is blank. Every value travels as text, whatever the setting's declared type says, because that is the shape of the column it lands in. A boolean is the word 'true' or the word 'false'; an i18n message and a list of sections are JSON. The API checks each against its type and refuses the whole request if any one of them does not fit.
